body:
The UI/UX tab shows a design as rendered screens, built from a tree of components that an agent can read exactly. Depends on feature:9d778f6e03dea799 for the page and records.

## Asked for

- UI/UX is one of the Design page's two tabs.
- The first version covers the component tree and its rendering. Attachments such as raster and SVG images come later.
- The human is drawn to Gleam's Elmish approach (Lustre) for three reasons: it can be displayed inside Solace, it carries over directly to the apps being built, and it could produce an interactive mockup.
- Use the same technology the app will be built with, including for styling.
- An element's position lives on its parent, so children move when their parent moves.
- Agents are fluent in the design's representation, which means not relying on CSS.
- Eventually the tab supports drag and drop and WYSIWYG editing (feature: direct editing).

## From the other agent's plan (direction, not gospel)

- Screens are component trees, with an ID on every element.
- A default palette of Lustre components built into Solace.
- Layout comes from row and column containers: direction, gap, padding, align and justify. Sizes are fill, hug or fixed.
- Styling is a default theme of tokens, component variants, and per-element overrides from a closed set of properties: fill, border, text color, size and padding. Each takes a token or a literal value.
- `action` names and `navigates_to` links make the preview a click-through prototype.
- The renderer puts a `data-design-id` on every element it outputs. Pointing depends on this (feature: notes).

## Decided

- The element is the primitive; see feature:9d778f6e03dea799.
- A design is data, not code, and is reference material; see the milestone. Solace does not generate code from it. Rendering it inside Solace is still wanted, because that is how a human sees it.
- There is no text editor. A screen is created and changed by the design agent until direct editing exists.

## Open

- Which components the default palette holds.
- What the default theme's tokens are, and how a project's own look is represented. An editable theme and a project's own component library are left out for now.

## Not in this feature

From the milestone's Left out list: grid and stack containers; sticky, scroll and overflow; screen states and mock data; attachments; an editable theme with "promote to token"; a project's own component library as the palette. Grid and stack are new container types that don't change the existing format, so they can arrive whenever a real screen needs one.
title: design: UI/UX tab
